question: Which hormone causes the ureters to relax and slows down urine flow during pregnancy?
explanation: Progesterone relaxes smooth muscles all over the body during pregnancy, which slows down urine movement through the ureters. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T2#BMP216_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why is kidney infection (pyelonephritis) more common on the right side during pregnancy?

options.A: Progesterone receptors are clustered more heavily around the right kidney.
options.B: The growing uterus tilts slightly to the right and presses more on the right ureter.
options.C: The right kidney is smaller and lacks natural protection.
options.D: Bacteria naturally gather on the right side of the urinary tract first.

explanation: The pregnant uterus tends to lean slightly to the right, putting extra pressure on the right ureter and causing urine to back up. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T2#BMP216_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which germ is responsible for most cases of kidney infections (pyelonephritis)?
explanation: Escherichia coli normally lives in the bowel and has special surface structures that help it stick to the urinary tract lining. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T2#BMP216_U1_T2_h2)

question: A pregnant patient with alkaline urine and a history of kidney stones develops a urinary infection. Which organism is most likely the cause?
explanation: Proteus species produce an enzyme called urease that breaks down urea into ammonia, creating an alkaline environment where kidney stones form easily. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T2#BMP216_U1_T2_h2)

question: What physical exam finding is most typical for a patient with acute pyelonephritis?
explanation: Tapping gently over the back where the kidneys sit causes sharp pain because the outer covering of the kidney is inflamed and stretched. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T2#BMP216_U1_T2_h3)

question: Why do many patients with a severe kidney infection feel very nauseous and vomit?

options.A: Kidney failure stops the pancreas from making digestive enzymes.
options.B: Antibiotics taken before admission upset the stomach lining.
options.C: High fever directly damages the lining of the small intestine.
options.D: Inflammation around the kidney irritates nearby nerves connected to the digestive tract.

explanation: The kidneys share nerve pathways with the digestive system, so severe kidney inflammation frequently triggers nausea and vomiting. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T2#BMP216_U1_T2_h3)

question: Which specific finding on a urine test shows that an infection has reached the kidneys rather than staying in the bladder?
explanation: Casts are tiny mold-like shapes formed inside the kidney tubules, so finding white blood cell casts proves the infection is located inside the kidneys. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T2#BMP216_U1_T2_h4)

question: What minimum bacterial count in a clean-catch urine sample usually confirms a urinary tract infection?
explanation: A count of 10^5 CFU/mL or higher is the standard threshold indicating an actual infection rather than normal skin contamination. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T2#BMP216_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why are pregnant women with acute pyelonephritis usually admitted to the hospital?

options.A: To perform immediate surgery to remove the affected kidney
options.B: To restrict all fluid intake until the infection clears
options.C: To give general anesthesia during urine collection
options.D: To prevent severe maternal infection spread and early labor using intravenous treatment

explanation: Pregnancy lowers the body's resistance, making hospital admission and IV antibiotics necessary to quickly control the infection and protect the baby. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T2#BMP216_U1_T2_h5)

question: When is it generally safe to switch a hospitalized kidney infection patient from intravenous antibiotics to pills?

options.A: Right after the very first dose of IV medication
options.B: Whenever the patient asks to go home
options.C: After the patient has been fever-free and stable for 48 hours
options.D: Only after a repeat urine test comes back completely clear

explanation: Waiting for 48 hours of normal temperature and stability ensures the infection is responding well before switching to oral medications. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T2#BMP216_U1_T2_h5)

question: How can a severe kidney infection in pregnancy trigger early labor?

options.A: Inflammation and high fevers trigger chemical signals that cause uterine contractions.
options.B: Oral antibiotics weaken the bag of waters from the outside.
options.C: The physical weight of the infected kidney pushes the baby downward.
options.D: Dehydration causes the placenta to separate from the uterine wall.

explanation: Severe systemic infection and fever release inflammatory chemicals like prostaglandins, which irritate the uterus and cause contractions. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T2#BMP216_U1_T2_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a major baby-related complication linked to untreated maternal kidney infections?

options.B: Fetal distress from maternal low oxygen

explanation: While pyelonephritis causes serious issues like preterm labor and growth restriction, it does not directly cause structural birth defects like missing limbs. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T2#BMP216_U1_T2_h6)

question: What is the main goal of routine urine testing during early pregnancy antenatal visits?

options.A: To measure daily food and nutrient intake
options.B: To confirm the exact age of the pregnancy
options.C: To check for underlying gestational diabetes
options.D: To find and treat silent bacteria in the urine before they turn into a kidney infection

explanation: Screening catches hidden bladder infections early so they can be treated before bacteria travel up to cause severe kidney infections. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T2#BMP216_U1_T2_h7)

question: A pregnant client asks a midwife how to help prevent kidney infections. What is the best advice?

options.A: Drink plenty of water and empty your bladder often without holding urine.
options.B: Avoid all physical exercise and stay in bed for the whole pregnancy.
options.C: Limit fluids after 4:00 PM to rest your kidneys overnight.
options.D: Take a strong antibiotic pill every morning at breakfast just in case.

explanation: Good hydration and regular urination flush out bacteria naturally, stopping them from multiplying and traveling up the urinary tract. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T2#BMP216_U1_T2_h7)
